items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: But I learned from him how to construct -- how to support a soloist, you know.

ctx.x: Well, did you learn much from him? I mean, did you spend much time with him, or --

Well, I didn't learn any -- what's the name, technical things from him, as far as playing the bass. But I learned from him how to construct -- how to support a soloist, you know. How to work with a rhythm section. And that was the first thing that became so disgusting with me when our rhythm section had to break up, and I had to come here to New York and work with various drummers and piano players every night, you know. And see that these guys didn't have the restraint.

What he showed me most of all was restraint, you know. I had to stand back there in that door -- this door was like leading to the alleyway, where he had to stand. But most of the time they had it closed. I'd stand right back there, right next to him, and he'd tell me, he'd say, now, there's a whole lots of things I could do here, but what you must do is play a straight line, because that man out there's waiting for this food from you, you know. And so he said, you could run all the changes, you could run changes…
